chunks: From him, from Fadala, from al-'Ala' and al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the legal rulings, and he said: 'In every religion, there is that by which they administer oaths.'

key_terms.يَسْتَحْلِفُونَ: they administer oaths / they cause to swear

ai.seo_question: What are the valid objects for oaths in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential principle that oaths are culturally and religiously contextual, acknowledging that each faith possesses specific sanctities invoked in swearing. In Shia legal theory, this supports the distinction between *al-yamin al-ghamus* (the perjurious oath) and other forms, emphasizing that the validity and gravity of an oath depend on the specific entity sworn upon according to the jurist's understanding. It underscores the flexibility in Islamic law to accommodate local customs while maintaining theological integrity regarding what constitutes a valid oath.
